chapter_title: Multimedia Storyboarding and AI Asset Generation
title: Signaling and Segmenting in Practice
description: AIL 606 textbook section connecting signaling and segmenting in practice to storyboard frame sequence with narration, signaling, and reader-action notes, reader notes, support moments, and revision evidence.
learning_objectives: Apply the scarcity and contrast law of signaling: justify cuing exactly one element on a frame and name the cues withheld.
Run the seam test to place a learner-controlled segmentation break at a conceptual boundary, distinguishing segmenting from pagination and from auto-advance.
Treat a signaling cue as a cognitive-load expenditure and judge an AI-proposed cue against its processing cost for a named learner.
Tie cue count and segment count to learner expertise (novice versus near-expert, expertise reversal) and document calibration as restraint in the storyboard trace.
